items.text: Explain what EBS is and why EC2 instances need storage

Explain EBS persistence vs Instance Store ephemeral nature
Name all 5 EBS volume types and their use cases
Explain the difference between IOPS and Throughput with an example
Describe what an EBS Snapshot is and how incremental snapshots work
Explain the key differences between gp2 and gp3
Describe what formatting a disk means and why it is required
Launch an EC2 instance with a custom EBS volume size
Attach a new EBS volume to a running EC2 instance via the console
Use lsblk and df -h to inspect disk devices on Linux
Format a new EBS volume with XFS and mount it
Expand an existing EBS volume and grow the filesystem (growpart + xfs_growfs)
Take a manual EBS snapshot from the console
Create a new EBS volume from a snapshot
Identify and clean up orphaned EBS volumes to avoid surprise charges
Know which EBS type to choose for a given scenario (IOPS vs throughput vs cost)
Know EBS volume size ranges for all types
Know max IOPS per volume for gp2 (16,000) and io1 (64,000)

Know how to move a volume across AZs using snapshots
